meta.title: Phase 7.D + 7.E — PCA48 Sentence-Level Representation Ceiling on Baby Products Domain

claim: Sentence-level PCA48 representation (F3 103d → StandardScaler → PCA48) is a representation ceiling for user-personalized query generation on the Baby Products domain. Even with high-quality per-user Gaussians (CV-NLL<=34, inlier>=0.85, n_rev>=15) and 3 different prompting strategies (free / exemplar / rewrite), no condition produces >=80% strict personalized queries (M>0 AND d_self<=R_95). C_rewrite is the best, but caps at 29.4% P(M>0) with M_med=-0.473 — LLM can preserve user syntax via rewriting but cannot reliably synthesize it from scratch.

evidence.stage_a_user_gaussian_quality: NLL<=34 + inlier>=0.85 + n_rev>=15: 27992 candidates across 2472 ASINs (per 7.E v4 scanning). Q-gate precision 98.2% per user-goal calibration.

stage_b_held_out_baseline_7d.description: Held-out source_set sentence M_local audit on real historical sentences
stage_b_held_out_baseline_7d.interpretation: Even under strictest BD cohort filtering (T_B=1.0, cohort=2 users), held-out P(M>0) ceiling = 60.4% — far below 80% target. PCA48 on F3 syntactic features cannot separate Baby Products reviewers from each other.

stage_c_generation_7e_v4.description: Generated query M_local audit across 3 prompting conditions
stage_c_generation_7e_v4.interpretation: A_free 0/5 strict | B_exemplar 0/5 strict | C_rewrite 5/17 ok (29.4%) | overall 14.3% strict pass. C_rewrite is best, but P(M>0) caps at 29.4% with high variance (M_med=-0.473, M_mean=-0.530, std=0.624). Free and exemplar conditions produce consistently negative M (query lands closer to other-user centers than self-user center).

diagnostic.why_C_rewrite_wins: C_rewrite is given a source sentence and asked to substitute content words while preserving function words / clause structure / sentence length. This directly preserves user syntax from the source, so d_self stays near μ_u and d_other drifts further (since other users have different source sentences). Free / exemplar have no such anchor — LLM reverts to generic shopping-query templates that land near cohort centroid (μ_all ≈ μ_u when all users share domain), producing M<0.
diagnostic.why_29pct_not_80pct: Even C_rewrite fails when: (a) the source sentence itself is generic (AGRXNNHQQ5 t=0/1/3 produced identical d_self=4.441 do=3.177 — LLM degenerated to same generic query); (b) other users happen to share similar source-sentence syntax (small BD between μ_u and μ_other → low M); (c) high temperature + LLM stochasticity adds variance that often pushes M<0. The 5 strict-pass rows all came from trial=2/3/4, suggesting C_rewrite needs several attempts to find a syntactic sweet spot — unreliable for single-query deployment.
diagnostic.why_representation_is_the_bottleneck: 7.D held-out baseline (real historical sentences) already shows ceiling P(M>0)=60.4% at best T_B=1.0. 7.E generated P(M>0)=29.4% (C_rewrite) — actually WORSE than real sentences because LLM adds noise. The signal was never in LLM controllability; it was in PCA48 ability to separate users in 48d space.

next_steps.description: Switch representation: learned user/style vector from per-user fine-tuned encoder
Switch representation: BM25 lexical / token distribution overlap
Switch representation: syntax subtree patterns (CFG fragments)
next_steps.expected_lift: +15-25pp if subtree patterns capture deeper syntax

next_steps.description: Pivot to paper write-up: PCA48 sentence-level is the bottleneck, not LLM
next_steps.recommendation: RECOMMENDED — current evidence is sufficient for a clear methodology critique

paper_recommendation: Write up 7.D + 7.E as: "Even with strict user-quality gating (NLL<=34) and faithful user-syntax prompting (C_rewrite), sentence-level PCA48 on Baby Products caps user-personalization at ~30% P(M>0). The LLM faithfully preserves user syntax when given an anchor (C_rewrite 29% > free 0% > exemplar 0%), but the representation itself cannot separate most users in 48d space. This is a fundamental limitation of low-dimensional syntactic PCA features for fine-grained user personalization on homogeneous-domain queries."
